newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sumitomo closure of copper positions seen bullish.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo closure of copper positions seen bullish.

text.p: Japan's Sumitomo Corp's announcement on Thursday that it has liquidated most of its open copper positions is seen as bullish for world copper prices, Singapore traders said.
"You might see some panic buying coming in here," one said.
Three month London Metal Exchange copper prices were indicated at $1,948/$1,953 a tonne at 0705 GMT, up from around $1,939/$1,944 when Sumitomo made the statement in Tokyo.
"We're around the 10-day moving average at $1,940 and if we break this then we could be heading to test resistance at $2,020, which is a very good number," another trader said.

Sumitomo president Kenji Miyahara told a news conference that the company has liquidated most of its open uncovered copper positions, although it still has some long and short positions in the market.
Traders said copper should encounter some initial resistance in the $1,870/80 area and then at $2,000.
"Where it goes really depends on what the funds make of it. They were buying back copper overnight in New York and we saw some buying orders in Asia today," a trader said.
In late LME trade on Wednesday, three month copper was quoted at $1,935/38 a tonne versus $1,870 the previous day on a technical recovery seen at the start of the week.
Copper later staged a further surge in New York after speculative stops were triggered, helped by consumer and hedge buying.
